question: What are the two hourly volume thresholds in All-Way Stop Control Warrant D, and how can they be adjusted when the major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not contain the actual volume threshold values from Items A and B of Paragraph 1 of Section 2B.16 (the All-Way Stop Control Warrant D vehicular volume criteria), so the two specific hourly thresholds cannot be stated from this evidence. What the evidence does establish is the speed-based adjustment: when the major-street 85th-percentile approach speed exceeds 40 mph, those minimum vehicular volume warrants may be reduced to 70 percent of their stated values. Options (permitted): - "If the 85th-percentile approach speed of the major-street traffic exceeds 40 mph, the minimum vehicular volume warrants may be reduced to 70 percent of the values given in Items A and B in Paragraph 1 of this Section." Citations: - Section 2B.16 Option §2 (p.79) Note: The remaining evidence (Sections 4C.02, 4C.03, 4C.05, and 4C.08) concerns traffic signal warrants, not All-Way Stop Control Warrant D, and does not supply the missing threshold values.
gold_answer: For the same 8 hours of a typical day, the combined entering volume must be at least 300 units per hour on the major-street approaches and at least 200 units per hour on the minor-street approaches. If the major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph, the minimums may be reduced to 70 percent of those values.
